learningObjectives: Choose Field Types that capture and format Case information correctly
Configure functions, expressions and Decision tables for calculated values
Explain how calculation networks update dependent fields
Configure Views to collect, present and reuse Case information

elements.description: A named, reusable UI component that stores a value associated with a Case. The field name and stored value form a data element. Its Field Type controls the kind of information stored and its display format.

elements.text: Fields and Views work like a spreadsheet: each field is a labelled cell holding one value for the Case, a calculated field is a formula cell, and a View arranges the cells a user needs for one task. The same stored value can appear in several Views without being entered twice.

elements.description: Determines the information stored and how it is formatted. Pega predicts a type from the field name and defaults to Text (single line), but the author must verify the type before submitting.
Choose the type for the business value, not for its appearance:
items: Simple types: Text (single line or paragraph), Boolean, Currency, Date & time, Date only, Time only, Decimal, Integer, Percentage, Email, Phone, URL, Picklist, Address, User reference and Prediction
Email, Phone and URL are action-oriented: the stored value is displayed as a link that opens mail, a phone call or the browser
Fancy types: Attachment stores documents or files; Location accepts an address or automatic geolocation
Prediction requires decision nodes (Pega Process AI); Address shows country-specific fields after the Country selection
An Integer stores the value from its first non-zero digit. Use Text for numeric-looking values that need no arithmetic, such as identifiers with leading zeros

elements.description: A calculation sets a field from one or more input fields, for example an item total from unit price and quantity. Calculation occurs whenever a user updates an input, which removes manual arithmetic and reduces errors.

Each calculation joins the application's calculation network. A calculated field can feed another calculation, so one input change (such as item quantity) can update several dependent fields. Whether users may override a result is a separate View design decision.

App Studio offers three approaches. Functions Sum of, Average of, Maximum of and Minimum of iterate over items in a data relationship and support Decimal, Currency and Integer fields. Expressions combine simple fields, fancy fields and data relationships. Decision tables test field values and return a result.

Reference fields with the dot operator, which lists fields available in the current Case; prefix a field with its data relationship when needed. Operators include + - * /, parentheses, Boolean AND and OR. Text can be concatenated with quoted static text. Expressions are available for every simple type except Email, Phone and Picklist.

elements.term: Decision tables and where calculations live
elements.description: Create a custom decision table in App Studio only in a Constellation application, or reference a Dev Studio decision table that a System Architect has marked as a relevant record. Calculated fields are added on the Data model tab of either a Case Type or a data object, depending on the use case.

A reusable configuration of fields and other UI elements that collects or displays information. A View states what users need to see and when; Pega supplies a consistent, responsive presentation. Each field and its value is a data element that can be shown editable or read-only.

A form is a View that collects user input and processes work, usually with submit, cancel or navigation actions; not every View is a form. A Multi-step Form splits many fields into several focused Views. Other Views show read-only summaries or confirmations. For each task choose the fields, value types and order, and whether each field is editable or read-only, visible or hidden, required or optional.

elements.caption: A form is a type of View, but not all Views are forms. Constellation also names View types such as Form, List, Full page and Partial; those categories come from Constellation documentation rather than this module topic.

elements.title: Field Type & View Design Decisions

examPitfalls.title: Pick the Field Type for the data shape
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Text (single line) accepts any line of text. When a value has a known shape, such as a fixed list, a yes/no answer, money or a date, Text loses the validation and display format the matching type provides.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Fixed options → Picklist; yes/no → Boolean; money → Currency; calendar date → Date only. Keep Text for numeric-looking identifiers that need no arithmetic, such as values with leading zeros.

examPitfalls.title: Calculated value vs. default value
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A default value only proposes a starting value. A calculated value is recalculated whenever a user updates one of its input fields, and dependent calculations follow through the calculation network.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Derived from other fields → calculation; common starting value that users may change → default value.

examPitfalls.title: View editability
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A form can mix editable decision fields with read-only information collected earlier. Do not treat every field in a View as having the same editability.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Configure field editability, visibility and required status for the user's task.

examPitfalls.title: Field and property
examPitfalls.trapDescription: App Studio says field; Dev Studio shows the same definition as a property rule. Treating them as two separate artifacts leads to wrong answers about where a field is defined.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: App Studio fields correspond to property definitions. Constellation Views are not interchangeable with Traditional UI Section/Harness rules.

examPitfalls.title: Protect a system-maintained result
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A requirement may prohibit manual override of a computed result. Configure read-only presentation for that requirement; calculation alone is not a universal editability rule.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Make the output read-only where the system must remain authoritative, and test input changes and dependent results.

examPitfalls.title: Views are reusable
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Views are reusable configurations. A View defined on a shared data object can be referenced wherever that object is used, instead of rebuilding the same layout per Case Type.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Define the View where its fields live and reference it from consumers; rule resolution and context decide which version each consumer gets.

examPitfalls.title: Calculation behavior and persistence are separate
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The calculation network updates dependent values when an input changes. This does not establish whether a property is persisted or whether elapsed time alone refreshes it.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Verify calculation dependencies, triggers and persistence requirements in the actual implementation.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A field must let users pick exactly one shipping speed from a fixed set of three values (Standard, Express, Overnight). The list rarely changes and is defined inside the application. Which Field Type best enforces this controlled, single-choice list?

options.text: Picklist — enforces a defined list of allowed values and constrains the user to one selection
Text (single line) with a placeholder listing the three options — guides the user but does not prevent them typing anything else
Data reference to an external Shipping data object — appropriate when options are sourced from an external system, but overkill for three fixed in-app values
Multi-select Picklist — presents the list but allows multiple selections, violating the 'exactly one' requirement

practiceQuiz.hint: Fixed, in-app list + exactly one choice — which type enforces both?
practiceQuiz.rationale: A Picklist offers a list of predefined values and the field holds one selection. A Text placeholder only suggests values, a separate data object is unnecessary for three in-app values, and multiple selections break the one-speed rule.

optionExplanations.A: A Picklist restricts shipping speed to one of the defined choices.
optionExplanations.B: A placeholder suggests values but does not enforce the permitted list.
optionExplanations.C: A separately maintained shipping object is unnecessary for this fixed in-app list.
optionExplanations.D: Multiple selections would violate the one-speed requirement.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA must configure a 'Line Total' field on a purchase order. It must always equal Quantity × Unit Price, recalculate automatically when either input changes, and be prevented from manual user editing. Which combination achieves this?

options.text: Calculated value driven by an arithmetic expression (Quantity × Unit Price), presented read-only so users cannot override the system-maintained value
A text field with a default value of '0' that the user can overwrite if Quantity or Price is updated manually
An editable Currency field with a validation rule that checks Quantity × Unit Price = Line Total on submit
A Decision Table that returns the correct Line Total when given the Quantity and Unit Price as inputs, displayed as an editable field

practiceQuiz.hint: The key requirements are: auto-compute, recalculate on change, and prevent editing.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The expression maintains the total from its inputs, and read-only presentation meets the explicit no-override requirement. A default or submit-time validation alone does not maintain this result as inputs change.

optionExplanations.A: The expression recalculates Line Total and read-only presentation prevents manual overrides.
optionExplanations.B: A default zero is not a calculation and does not track changing inputs.
optionExplanations.C: Validation detects an inconsistent total but does not itself maintain the value.
optionExplanations.D: An editable output still permits an override even if the table computes correctly.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A new SA asks what a View actually does in a Constellation application. Which statement correctly describes the role of a View?

options.text: A UI component that gathers data from, or displays data to, the user for the current Step or Case
A rule that persists Case data to the database when the Case is saved
A reusable business-logic rule that calculates field values from conditions
A routing rule that determines which user or queue receives the Assignment

practiceQuiz.hint: A View lives in the UI layer — collect or show data. What do the others belong to?
practiceQuiz.rationale: A View is a UI-layer component that collects input from or displays data to the user for the current Step/Case. Views define presentation — they don't persist data or execute business logic.

optionExplanations.A: The View defines the fields and instructions used to collect or show Case information.
optionExplanations.B: Database persistence belongs to Case/data processing, not the View definition.
optionExplanations.C: Calculation rules provide logic; a View presents the resulting fields.
optionExplanations.D: Routing determines the assignee rather than the layout or data displayed.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A developer who built fields in App Studio switches to Dev Studio to inspect them at the rule level. Under what name do those App Studio 'fields' appear in Dev Studio?

options.text: A property
A Field Value
A Data Page
A Data Transform

practiceQuiz.hint: App Studio 'field' is the friendly name for one specific Dev Studio rule type.
practiceQuiz.rationale: An App Studio 'field' is a Property rule in Dev Studio — same artifact, different name. A Field Value rule stores a localized text string (e.g., a picklist label), not the data element itself.

optionExplanations.A: Dev Studio represents the App Studio field as a property rule.
optionExplanations.B: A Field Value supplies localized values or labels rather than defining this property.
optionExplanations.C: A Data Page retrieves data; it is not the field definition.
optionExplanations.D: A Data Transform maps or initializes values rather than defining the field.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A 'Total Premium' field is calculated from base premium × risk factor. The business forbids users from changing the result. Why present it read-only?

options.text: The system maintains the value from its inputs; an editable field would let a user overwrite the calculated result
Read-only fields are skipped during validation, which makes the form submit faster
Constellation has no editable control for calculated values, so read-only is the only option that renders
A field must be read-only before any other field's calculation is allowed to reference it

practiceQuiz.hint: What goes wrong if a user can type over a system-calculated value?
practiceQuiz.rationale: The scenario requires the formula to remain authoritative. Read-only presentation protects that result from manual override; this is a design requirement rather than a claim that every calculated property has the same UI settings.

optionExplanations.A: Read-only presentation keeps the formula result authoritative for Total Premium.
optionExplanations.B: Read-only display does not universally exempt data from validation.
optionExplanations.C: This is a data-integrity design decision, not evidence of a missing rendering control.
optionExplanations.D: Calculation dependencies do not require every input to be presented read-only.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A form must capture 'Has the customer agreed to the terms and conditions?' — the answer is either yes or no, stored as a property, and should use a Boolean input control in Constellation. A junior SA configures it as Text (single line). What is the problem, and what is the correct field type?

options.text: Text (single line) stores an arbitrary string — users could type 'maybe'; a Boolean (True/False) field correctly constrains the value, uses a Boolean control, and stores a valid yes/no
The issue is not the field type but the missing validation rule — add an Edit Validate that allows only 'Yes' or 'No' as text values
Text (single line) is correct for checkboxes in Constellation — the Constellation UI layer automatically converts any text field to a toggle control when the field is used in a form
Use an Integer field (0 for No, 1 for Yes) — Pega's Boolean implementation has a known rendering bug in Constellation that Text or Integer avoids

practiceQuiz.hint: Boolean is the semantically correct type for a binary yes/no value.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Boolean represents the two-state consent value and uses the appropriate Boolean input control. Text stores arbitrary strings rather than the intended typed true/false value.

optionExplanations.A: Boolean matches the two-state consent value; use the appropriate Boolean control.
optionExplanations.B: Restricting text strings does not change the underlying property into Boolean.
optionExplanations.C: A text field does not automatically acquire Boolean semantics when placed on a form.
optionExplanations.D: The asserted platform defect is unsupported; use the type matching the business value.

practiceQuiz.scenario: On the Workflow tab, an SA clicks 'Configure View' for a Step so users can enter information at that point in the process. Which View type is created to collect that input?

options.text: Form View — collects user input and is configured per Step
Partial View: a reusable fragment that is embedded in other Views
Full Page View: a full-page layout such as a Case summary
List View: displays multiple records in a table

practiceQuiz.hint: Which View type is for data entry (not display) at a single Step?
practiceQuiz.rationale: A Form View supports the requested input task. It can contain editable and read-only fields; the cited Constellation guidance distinguishes it from display-oriented Views.

optionExplanations.A: A Form View provides the input fields required for the Assignment at this Step.
optionExplanations.B: An embedded fragment is not the Step form that collects this input.
optionExplanations.C: A Case summary display does not provide the required Assignment input form.
optionExplanations.D: A table of many records is not the data entry for this single Step.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA is reviewing Pega's field configuration options and wants to confirm which statements about Field Types are accurate. Which TWO statements about Field Types in Pega are correct?

options.text: The Field Type identifies the type of information the system stores for the field
Assigning the right Field Type helps users provide valid information and displays data in the correct format
Field Type only affects how a value is displayed, not the format in which it is stored
Field Type can be changed freely after data exists, with no data-conversion impact

practiceQuiz.hint: Two true statements about what Field Type actually governs.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Field Type identifies the information stored and, through that, supports valid input and correct formatting. It is more than a display setting, and changing the type of a populated field needs a data review.

optionExplanations.A: The Fields topic defines Field Type as identifying the type of information stored.
optionExplanations.B: The topic states that the type ensures valid input and the correct display format.
optionExplanations.C: Type affects the value representation as well as its presentation.
optionExplanations.D: Changing a populated field type can require conversion and compatibility review.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The team configured a List View only for displaying records and provided no create action. Users can browse but cannot add records. What explains this behavior?

options.text: Displaying a record list does not itself configure the required create interaction and permissions
Editing is blocked because the users lack the Edit privilege on this Case Type
A List View can never be made editable under any configuration
The List View must be backed by a Savable Data Page before any records can be added

practiceQuiz.hint: Look at what the team actually configured for the list.
practiceQuiz.rationale: This scenario explicitly supplies a display-only configuration. A record list does not automatically supply a create workflow, data persistence or permissions; configure and test those capabilities separately.

optionExplanations.A: The stated configuration provides display without the required create interaction.
optionExplanations.B: The missing create interaction is explicit; the scenario does not establish a privilege failure.
optionExplanations.C: The default display behavior is not a universal prohibition on supported editing.
optionExplanations.D: A Data Page requirement does not by itself explain the explicitly missing create interaction.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A field's value must depend on combinations of conditions — for example, a discount rate determined by customer tier AND region. Besides a formula expression, which rule type can compute and return that value declaratively?

options.text: A Decision Table — maps combinations of conditions to result values
A Validate rule — asserts that data is correct but returns no computed value
A Data Page — sources and caches data, but does not derive a value from condition combinations
An Edit Validate — checks a single field's format and returns true/false, not a tiered value

practiceQuiz.hint: Which rule maps 'these conditions → this value'?
practiceQuiz.rationale: A Decision Table maps combinations of conditions (tier × region) to output values — the declarative tool for this exact pattern. Validation rules check input correctness; they don't compute output values.

optionExplanations.A: A Decision Table maps tier and region conditions to the calculated discount result.
optionExplanations.B: Validation checks acceptability rather than calculating the discount mapping.
optionExplanations.C: A Data Page can source a result but is not the condition table requested.
optionExplanations.D: Edit Validate tests a field value rather than returning a tier-and-region discount.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After a customer submits an incident report through a form, the application shows a read-only confirmation of what was reported. Which statement about this design is correct?

options.text: The confirmation is a View that is not a form: a form is one type of View, and Views can also display read-only information
The confirmation must be a form, because every View collects user input
A read-only confirmation cannot be a View; it must be built outside the Case
The confirmation must reuse the submission form with every field still editable

practiceQuiz.rationale: A form is a View for collecting input and processing work, but not all Views are forms. A View can present a read-only summary or confirmation after submission.

optionExplanations.A: The Views topic says a form is a type of View but not all Views are forms, citing a read-only confirmation as the example.
optionExplanations.B: Views both collect and display information; a summary does not have to collect input.
optionExplanations.C: Displaying a read-only summary is one of the stated purposes of a View.
optionExplanations.D: A confirmation shows what was submitted; keeping the fields editable does not fit its purpose.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA designs an 'Address' View on the shared Address data object and references it from several Case Types instead of rebuilding it each time. Why is designing Views for reuse considered best practice?

options.text: A View built once can be referenced across multiple Case Types, so a single update propagates everywhere — saving effort and ensuring consistency
Reusable Views render faster because Pega caches them at the node level
A View must be reused because it can only be bound to one field at a time
Only reusable Views support model-driven controls; single-use Views fall back to manual HTML

practiceQuiz.hint: What is the maintenance payoff of one View referenced many times?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Create the reusable View in the appropriate data-object class and embed it in consumers. This reduces duplicate layouts; rule resolution and context still determine which version each consumer uses.

optionExplanations.A: Shared View definitions reduce duplication and make updates consistent for consumers.
optionExplanations.B: Reuse alone does not guarantee node-level caching or faster rendering.
optionExplanations.C: A View can contain several fields; reuse is not imposed by a one-field restriction.
optionExplanations.D: A single-use View still uses the platform presentation model.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An order total must be stored as money and displayed with the application's default currency symbol. Which Field Type fits best?

options.text: Currency: stores the value and currency symbol based on the default currency type
Decimal: stores numbers with a fractional part but does not identify a currency
Text (single line) — accepts any characters, with no monetary validation or formatting
Integer — stores whole numbers only and cannot represent cents/decimals

practiceQuiz.hint: Which type is defined specifically for money?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Currency stores currency symbols and values based on the default currency type. Decimal supports fractions without a currency, Text has no numeric semantics, and Integer cannot hold cents.

optionExplanations.A: Currency stores the symbol and value based on the default currency type.
optionExplanations.B: Decimal supports fractional numbers but does not by itself identify a currency.
optionExplanations.C: Freeform text lacks the required numeric monetary semantics.
optionExplanations.D: Integer cannot represent a fractional monetary amount such as cents.

practiceQuiz.scenario: To tailor exactly what a user sees and enters at a particular Step, what does the SA add to that Step's View?

options.text: Fields — each with an appropriate Field Type; fields are the building blocks of a View's UI
Stages — which structure the Case life cycle, not the contents of a single View
Routing rules — which determine who receives the Assignment, not what the View displays
Access Roles — which control permissions, not the composition of a View

practiceQuiz.hint: A View's UI is built from which atomic elements?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Fields with appropriate types are the data elements added to a View. Stages structure workflow, routing chooses the assignee, and Access Roles define permissions.

optionExplanations.A: Fields with suitable types supply the values shown or entered in the Step View.
optionExplanations.B: Stages organize the workflow rather than the fields in this View.
optionExplanations.C: Routing selects who performs the work rather than composing the display.
optionExplanations.D: Access Roles define permissions rather than the View layout.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A developer is configuring a Calculated Value field for a total price in an order entry Case. Which TWO statements correctly describe Calculated Values in Pega?

options.text: A Calculated Value uses a formula to derive its value automatically from other fields in the Case
When users must not override the result, the calculated field should be presented read-only
Calculated Values can be edited directly by users alongside automatic recalculation
Calculated Values replace Data Pages as the mechanism for storing derived data in a Case

practiceQuiz.hint: A calculation derives the value; the View decides whether users may change it.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Functions, expressions and Decision tables can calculate values from other data. For this system-maintained total, read-only presentation prevents manual override. Calculations and Data Pages serve different responsibilities.

optionExplanations.A: A calculated value derives the total from the configured input relationship.
optionExplanations.B: Read-only presentation protects the system-maintained result from manual override.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is defining fields for a customer profile that captures first name, date of birth, and annual income. Which TWO field type choices are appropriate for this scenario?

options.text: Text (Single-line) — for the customer's first name
Date only: for the customer's date of birth
Integer — for the customer's first name to track its character length
URL — for the customer's annual income to link to external financial records

practiceQuiz.hint: Match each field type to the nature of the data — text for names, date for calendar values.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Text (single line) suits a short name. Date only stores a calendar date such as date of birth. Integer stores whole numbers, not names, and URL stores web addresses, not income.

optionExplanations.A: A first name is a short string suited to a single-line Text field.
optionExplanations.B: A date of birth is a calendar date, which Date only stores with a localized format.
optionExplanations.C: A numeric length does not preserve the actual customer name.
optionExplanations.D: A web address does not represent the annual income amount.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA needs to design a Claims application screen that allows adjusters to edit a single claim and also view a list of prior claims. Which TWO View type characteristics guide the selection of the appropriate View for each purpose?

options.text: Form Views are designed for capturing and editing data for a single Case record
List Views display a collection of records in a structured grid and are suited for summarizing or browsing multiple records
Form Views always render as full-page overlays and cannot be embedded within other Views
List Views support real-time inline editing for all field types by default in Constellation applications

practiceQuiz.hint: Form Views are for single-record data entry; List Views are for displaying collections of records.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Use a Form View for the current claim input interaction and a List View for browsing previous claims. Supported list actions and editing must be explicitly configured; they are not automatically enabled for every field.

optionExplanations.A: A Form View supports entering or editing the fields for the current claim.
optionExplanations.B: A List View suits browsing the collection of previous claims.
optionExplanations.C: Form Views are not defined by an always-overlay restriction.
optionExplanations.D: Supported editing must be configured; it is not enabled for every field by default.

quickRecap.value: Named, reusable UI component; stores one value per Case. Name + value = data element. App Studio field = Dev Studio property.
Identifies the stored information and display format. Predicted from the name, default Text (single line); verify before Submit.
Set from input fields by a function, expression or decision table; recalculates when an input changes, through the calculation network.
Reusable configuration of fields and UI elements that collects or displays information. A form is a View for input; not every View is a form.
Per field: editable or read-only, visible or hidden, required or optional. One View can mix read-only and editable fields.
